answer: Admission is a written act, not a username. Each applicant signs a live prompt with a hardware-bound quill whose stroke timing is published as a one-way sketch; a copied key can replay the bytes but not the timing, and a mismatch burns the 400-token bond. Three members of a rotating grove, none chosen by the applicant, must co-sign that sketch on consecutive days before a single narrow inlet accepts one new key per sponsor per epoch. A farm of 150 aliases needs 150 distinct stroke histories and 450 independent co-signers; reused timing or shared sponsors fuse the cluster and slash every seat.
